change: OriginalDeferredRelease (NTSDRuntime): one lazily started thread, NTSD.release (utility QoS; the Android host pins it to the slowest tier, like the presenter), takes values whose last reference the caller hands over (retire, consuming) and frees them. complete(first:) retires the cycle's outcome and the body's PendingReturn after the Host's tail commits (they hold the last references to their State copies then); finish() retires the drained batches after performing them; the menu step retires the driver it made. A backlog beyond 256 values is freed by the caller. The game never observes when Swift frees a value

The retire moved after the drain loop; the 7 loading tests then passed in debug, and the comment forbids consuming an outer variable from a defer

review: independent read-only review: approve with nits (no game-observable change; on a committed step the platform's receipt histories keep every resource alive; after a failed step a retired driver may free a new window lease or display storage, whose deinits already run on any thread). Applied: retire takes its value consuming and callers move it (no deinit can land on the caller); the comment states the throw-path case; a backlog cap; nonisolated(unsafe) threadStart; tests for the hook and the backlog; a TSan run
